articles.title: How do I spot a non-genuine (parts built) APIM?
articles.body:
Great question! It used to be pretty easy years ago since they didn't have any of the typical stickers on them. Now they're pretty great at creating fake labels to stick on the APIM modules to make them look authentic. If you didn't know what to look for, you might not be able to tell the difference. I've seen numerous YouTube installation videos where people said their hardware looked "pretty legit" even though it was clearly fake. Let us help you tell the difference. These are some of the most common examples. For the record, we do not use these.

Examples to compare

Perfect example of an APIM that's a fake, no label!

Another perfect example, no label

Now we're getting into fake label territory. The part number for this module starts with a J which would signify that this module came from a 2018 vehicle. However, in 2018 Ford removed the 2nd redundant USB port on the back (it would be blank, they covered it with metal in 2019). The label looks really good, so the case might be authentic, but the PCB inside doesn't belong in that case. The problem here is that you don't want to purchase hardware from a 2016 vehicle (due to reliability reasons) so you wouldn't have any idea what you're getting here.

Here's one that I don't see as often. The label and the case look okay, however it has these quality check stickers on it from a Chinese reseller.

Here's another example of a fake label. In this case, it's using a part number that starts with H, which signifies a 2017. In 2017 these modules still should have that redundant USB port on the back, but this one doesn't have it. Also, if you take note of the MFG date, it says 2019.

Why we avoid 2016 modules

While we're at it, please beware of ALL modules from 2016, even if they're authentic. These modules have an issue where they're very prone to failure. We don't sell modules from 2016 at all. The part numbers on these will start with a G and usually end with a CM, BM, KL, etc. (but not always). There are two different sticker styles that come on them. Both are shown below.

An example from our inbox

We've even had people reach out to us on Facebook to try to sell us fake modules in bulk. See the screenshot below. Even if you're not buying from us, I hope this helps guide your purchasing decision in a positive direction. Please reach out if you have any questions, we would be happy to help you.

articles.title: Will my 2013–2014 F-150 Raptor’s front camera work after upgrading?
articles.body:
Yes — the factory front off road camera can still work after upgrading your 2013–2014 F-150 Raptor to Sync 3, but accessing it requires additional steps.

With the vehicle stationary, the area around it clear and your foot firmly on the brake:

  1. Turn Camera Delay on in the touchscreen’s camera settings.
  2. Enable off road mode and turn the front camera on through the vehicle apps menu.
  3. Shift into Reverse, wait a moment, then shift back into Neutral or Drive.

The camera’s operation may differ from how it worked with your original Sync 2 system.

If the camera does not appear, contact us with your order number and let us know whether the rear camera still works.

Reference: original Raptor upgrade discussion

articles.title: 4" to 8" Conversion Overview
articles.body:
Converting your vehicle from the 4” display to the 8” display is easy with SimplyMichigan! It can also save you a bunch of money since pre-built kits have the added cost of convenience. We don’t currently stock complete kits for every vehicle however we do carry the majority of the items you would need to convert and will supply you the programming necessary to make sure the job is done right. 

  • First step. Looking for a complete list of what you need for your vehicle? Please visit the "What do I need exactly for my conversion?" support article by clicking here.

Please note, all of the items below that we do carry for this conversion, they are located in our store. For a total price of the items we carry please add them in your cart. We don't send invoices or give total prices written/verbally as the prices do change from time to time (and most people don't purchase right away) and we can't take into account special promotions, sales tax (if applicable, for Michigan residents), shipping, etc. The total price of your conversion will depend on how much you spend on the other few parts to complete the upgrade.

  • We highly encourage you to review the other articles on our support page as they may contain valuable information that may help you with your project.
  • We stock most of the parts you'll need for this conversion, simply add the ones you would like to purchase from us to your cart. To visit our store's 4" to 8" conversion section, please click here.
  • Please do not purchase hardware from us unless you have sourced all of the other parts needed for your vehicle. If you find yourself over your head or unable to find a harness for your vehicle and need to return the hardware we retain 5% of the total price to cover the costs of the transaction fees per our return policy; further, the $80 programming charge is also non-refundable. Please read this entire article in its entirety. A good handful of people don't fully understand the scope of this conversion and end up returning the hardware due to not understanding this process.

Overview

For all conversions you will need either a ELM327 USB cable (OHP ELMConfig is a great brand) or a ScanTool OBDLink EX cable (recommended but more costly) to connect to your OBD2 port via your laptop, if you have a 2019+ vehicle, we recommend spending the extra money on the OBDLink EX. You will also need FORScan downloaded with at least a trial extended license activated. This is not optional, please don't think you can skip this step. It's strongly recommended that you familiarize yourself with FORScan before proceeding. 

You can get a free two month extended license (required) located here.

4” to 8” conversions may sometimes require wiring changes and/or repining of the connections for your center bezel, unless a custom wiring harness is purchased. We currently do not sell wiring harnesses unless it's included with a complete kit. 

We will supply you with instructions on how to upload the files required for your vehicle via e-mail. Don’t be intimidated! It’s a very straight forward task and requires you click some buttons a handful of times. We will email these files to you typically within 4 business days, if you don’t see the email from me please check your junk/spam folder as it may incorrectly get flagged. With certain vehicles, such as the Escape and Focus, there are more settings that may need to be changed in the CCC programming (in FORScan), we unfortunately can't provide files for this and need to be changed manually. 

How much should this conversion cost?

For the items we provide you should expect to pay around $700-$900, this is dependent on the items your vehicle requires (recessed displays cost more for example) and if you choose a factory navigation system, which will obviously cost more as well. The rest of the cost is in your hands based on how much you’ll spend on the conversion harness, the HVAC 8” radio bezel, etc.

Where do I buy the other parts I need?

Most often people will pick these up on eBay. If you search "4 to 8 conversion Sync 3 harness" in eBay a bunch of harnesses will pop up. Please ensure you read the description completely to make sure that the harness will work with your vehicle. Contacting the seller may help as well, they can offer recommendations for your vehicle. The control panels are usually readily available there as well. Finding one for $100-$200 would be a fair price. The first few you find may be $300-$500, don't purchase those. Those sellers are just fishing to see if anyone will bite. Keep digging, you'll find the fairly priced ones farther down the list. 

Parts List & General Information

For a complete list of the items you would need for your vehicle, please click here. For a quick guide, for a good majority of conversions this is the list of the items you would need:

Available at SimplyMichigan

  • Screen and APIM bundle (with or without factory navigation)
  • 4” to 8” programming (required purchase with hardware, non-refundable)
  • USB hub and GPS antenna (included with hardware as long as the conversion kit option is selected)
  • Screen brackets (we will typically have these for newer vehicles that could’ve came with Sync 3 from the factory, sometimes these brackets were used on older vehicles as well but not always)
  • USB extension cable (we carry these on our website, this extension cable includes special connectors on both ends to securely attach to the USB hub and APIM)

NOT Available at SimplyMichigan

  • 4” to 8” conversion harness (these can be found on eBay or other larger infotainment websites, but they typically will cost more)
  • HVAC 8” radio/dash bezel (these can be found at your local salvage yard or you can find them on eBay)


This is the typical list of items that your vehicle may require to do this conversion. Your vehicle may require a few more parts not listed above or it might not need nearly as many (typical with newer 2018+ vehicles). Please see our other support article for an exact list of items needed. Some vehicles (typically the Explorer) will require a new HVAC module as well, especially if you're switching between manual and automatic climate controls. The replacement HVAC module needs to be pulled from a matching vehicle model that originally had the 8” display from the factory. 

Other Information

  • When you checkout with us we will need to know if the bezel you purchased has automatic climate controls (will have an AUTO button on it) or if it’s just a manual climate bezel. If you don’t know or don’t have one yet, please choose manual and we can have adjustments made later to your programming files.
  • Once the purchase is made with the programming, the $80 fee isn't refundable. Please ensure you have a plan ready to do this conversion and hold off buying the hardware and programming until you’re ready. 
  • For newer 2019+ vehicles your conversion will cost slightly more as you will need the latest generation 4 module for your vehicle to ensure that the firmware will be correct. A good rule of thumb, you’ll want hardware from the same model year or newer. You may run into issues using older hardware in a newer vehicle.
  • We don't sell programming for hardware you purchased elsewhere. Usually when a problem arises, most people will point to the programming being the issue when in reality (in almost every case we've had) it's an issue with the conversion harness that was purchased or a mistake during the install (connectors not being connected properly is a very common issue that we've seen)

articles.title: Can I upgrade my Maverick to Sync 3?
articles.body:
A Maverick with the base infotainment system requires more than an APIM and screen swap to upgrade to Sync 3. The required hardware, wiring and programming depend on the vehicle’s year and factory equipment.

Non-Sync 3 Mavericks pose a challenge because the base Sync system offered in the XL and XLT trims doesn’t actually have an APIM module. Everything is run from the ACM instead. To upgrade, you would need to replace your ACM with one that came from a Maverick that had Sync 3 and add a custom harness to bridge the ACM and the APIM together.

We can provide the APIM and the programming if you wanted to go this route.

articles.title: How do I reset my Sync 3 system?
articles.body:
If Sync 3 freezes, responds slowly or behaves unexpectedly, start with a soft reset. If the problem continues and you can access Settings, try a master reset.

Park safely before starting. Do not interrupt an update that is in progress.

1. Soft reset — restart without erasing your settings

  1. Press and hold the radio Power button and Seek Up / Next Track button together.
  2. Keep holding until the screen goes black, usually about 5–10 seconds, then release.
  3. Allow Sync to restart and check whether the issue is resolved.

2. Master reset — clear personal settings

A master reset removes paired phones, saved destinations and personal preferences. It does not remove the vehicle programming we prepared for your APIM.

  1. With the vehicle parked and running in an open, well-ventilated area, disconnect USB devices.
  2. Open Settings → General → Master Reset.
  3. Read the confirmation and select Continue.
  4. Wait for the system to restart, then pair your phone again and check its connection permissions.

We also recommend a master reset after installing your replacement or upgraded Sync 3 system.

If the problem continues

A power reset may be appropriate, but battery and module-disconnection procedures vary by vehicle. Contact us before disconnecting hardware if you do not have the correct procedure.

Include your order number, vehicle’s year and model, symptoms and which resets you have completed.

articles.title: How do I update the software and/or maps?
articles.body:
Option 1 - Preferred Method

IMPORTANT: This procedure SHOULD NOT BE USED on 2020+ vehicles or modules from 2020+ vehicles. Doing this will result in bricking the module and it being unrecoverable. 

Not sure what year your module was from? If you remember the part number on the front of the module you can use that. The part number would look something similar to: HJ4R-14G370-ABC. In this example, the first letter signifies the year. G = 2016, H = 2017, J = 2018, K = 2019, L = 2020, M = 2021. If you purchased from us, you can always e-mail us and ask as well. We can look up your order for you. You'll need your order number or stock ID number. This only applies if your vehicles APIM module HAS NOT been replaced by Ford. If it has you will need to look at the manufacturing date next to the part number. If the part number starts with J for example (it could be any letter) and it was manufactured in 2021, then you will NOT be able to use this method.

Updating the software and/or maps on your APIM module is easy and free. Head on over to cyanlabs.net and download their program (windows only, if you are using a Mac you can use bootcamp or parallels to run Windows) and go through the steps as prompted. You'll enter in your vehicles information, Sync 3 version, etc. Then you'll select the Sync version you want to update to and maps version (if applicable). Click start and it will automatically download the files needed from the internet and install them on the flash drive for you. Once finished, all that you will need to do is insert it into your vehicle and wait about 15 minutes (non-navigation) or 25 minutes (navigation) for it to install. You'll want at least a 16GB flash drive to do this. 

Please note, once you're updated past SYNC 3.4.19274, you will need to downgrade your software before you're able to update it again.

Option 2 - Official Route

Alternatively, you can go the official route of updating the software by logging into your Ford Owner account (https://www.ford.com/support/), adding the donor vehicles VIN from the sticker that was on the module when you received it and downloading and transferring the files to a flash drive. Ford supplies instructions on how to do this. This only updates the software, not the maps. To update the maps you would head on over to https://syncnavigation.com/ford/home where you'll enter the donor vehicles VIN (NOT your VIN) to check for updates. In most cases Ford does charge you for map updates. In some cases they may be free for newer vehicles/hardware.

Option 3 - SimplyMichigan Infotainment Supplied USB Flash Drive

If you're intimated by this process and would rather have a USB flash drive prepared for you, we do have this service available for $39. It's purely a convenience though, everything being provided is something you can do for free yourself. Please note, 2020+ vehicles are not eligible for this update method either. For more information on this service, check out: https://simplymichigan.co/products/2022-Sync-3-Software-and-or-Maps-Update-p559340575

articles.title: How does my vehicle’s electrical architecture affect a Sync 3 upgrade?
articles.body:
Electrical architecture is the system your vehicle uses to connect its electronic modules and allow them to communicate. This includes the infotainment system, instrument cluster, climate controls and other equipment.

Different Ford vehicles use different electrical architectures. These differences affect the wiring and programming needed when upgrading from a base audio system or Sync 2 to Sync 3.

For most supported vehicles, we adjust the APIM programming to account for these differences. However, some older vehicles — particularly those using CGEA 1.2 — may have limitations in how certain features appear on the touchscreen.

One example is the on-screen notification that appears when you change the fan speed or temperature. These notifications may behave differently after the upgrade, even when the physical climate controls continue to work normally.

Vehicle architecture reference

The following groups reflect the applications covered by this guide. Entries marked “+” should not be taken to mean that every subsequent vehicle generation uses the same architecture.

CGEA 1.2CGEA 1.3C1CMA
2009–2014 F-1502015+ F-150Focus
2009–2014 Edge2015+ EdgeEscape
2011–2014 Explorer2015+ ExplorerS-Max
2009–2016 Super Duty2017+ Super DutyC-Max
2009+ Flex2015+ Mustang
2010+ Taurus

What does this mean for your upgrade?

A Sync 3 APIM needs programming that matches your vehicle’s architecture and equipment. Installing the hardware alone does not ensure that every feature will communicate correctly with the rest of the vehicle.

We account for your vehicle’s configuration when preparing your module. If retaining a particular touchscreen or climate-control feature is important to you, please contact us before ordering with your vehicle’s year and model.

articles.title: Why did I receive a single-port USB hub instead of a dual-port hub?
articles.body:
Some vehicles need a single port USB hub to retain the connection to another USB port elsewhere in the vehicle. Examples include certain 2015 Focus, 2015 Mustang and 2016 Explorer applications.

The single port hub has an additional connection on the back for that separate USB port. Using a dual port hub instead may prevent the other port from working with Apple CarPlay or Android Auto.

We select the hub based on your vehicle’s configuration. If you’re unsure whether you received the correct one, please contact us with your order number.

articles.title: What should I check if my vehicle has no sound?
articles.body:
No sound does not automatically mean your ACM or APIM needs replacing. Depending on your audio system, the issue may involve the ACM / receiver, amplifier, power supply, connections, wiring or speakers.

Start by checking what still works:

  • Can you open the Audio screen and change radio stations?
  • Is the problem limited to AM/FM, phone audio or both?
  • Are all speakers affected, or only certain ones?
  • Does your vehicle have standard audio or a branded system such as Sony, B&O, THX or Revel?
  • Did the problem begin after an installation, software update or battery work?

Next, try the speaker self test if your system supports it and you can access Audio/FM. Follow the instructions on our installation guides page and record which speaker positions play.

A silent position may indicate a speaker, wiring or amplifier-output problem. The test alone does not confirm which part has failed. If you cannot start the test, include that information when asking for help.

Contact us with what you observed, and we’ll help you work through the next checks before choosing a replacement.

articles.title: Why is my Sync 3 display flickering?
articles.body:
First, check whether the screen is switching between light and dark modes or whether the picture itself is flickering or cutting out. These symptoms can have different causes.

If it happens around dawn, dusk or when entering tunnels, check that nothing is covering the light sensor on your dashboard. Note whether the changes occur only as the surrounding light changes.

If the picture flickers in steady lighting, try a soft reset using our reset instructions.

If the issue continues, contact us before updating software or ordering a replacement display. Include your order number, vehicle’s year and model, and your Sync software version if you can access it.

A short video can help us understand what you’re seeing. You can attach it to your email reply after we respond.

articles.title: What should I do if I see a navigation fault message?
articles.body:
You can clear a navigation fault message through Sync 3’s diagnostic menu. With your vehicle parked and the system turned on:

  1. Press and hold the forward seek / skip track buttons on both the steering wheel and center dash at the same time for approximately five seconds.
  2. A speaker test will begin. You can skip it or let it finish.
  3. Select Testing Settings, scroll toward the bottom, and select Remove Navigation Fault.

If the message returns, check the GPS antenna connection and placement. Make sure the antenna supplied with your upgrade kit is firmly connected to the back of the APIM, with no metal directly above the antenna.

If you installed a different antenna, a matching connector alone does not mean it is compatible with Sync 3. Use the antenna supplied with your kit.

Clearing the message does not repair an antenna or connection problem. If the warning continues after these checks, please contact us with your order number, vehicle’s year and model, and the exact warning.

articles.title: Why does my GPS position jump around or point the wrong way?
articles.body:
After a Sync 2 to Sync 3 upgrade, some vehicles may receive conflicting location information from their original GPS equipment. Disconnecting the original GPS unit may resolve this problem.

First, check that the new GPS antenna supplied with your kit is firmly connected to the APIM and installed with no metal directly above it.

If the problem continues:

  1. Turn off the ignition before accessing the original GPS unit.
  2. Locate the original unit using the reference photo below. Depending on your vehicle, it may be behind the center of the dashboard or behind the instrument cluster. The trim removal steps vary by vehicle.
  3. Release the connector’s locking tab and unplug it from the original GPS unit. Pull on the connector, not the wires.
  4. Secure the disconnected connector so it cannot rattle, then reinstall any removed trim.
  5. Turn the system back on and check the map position outdoors, allowing time for the new antenna to acquire a GPS signal.

Leave the new GPS antenna connected to the Sync 3 APIM. These steps apply to the original GPS equipment retained during an upgrade, not the new antenna supplied with your kit.

articles.title: Why does the other person hear an echo during Android Auto calls?
articles.body:
If the person you’re calling hears their own voice echo, note whether it happens only with Android Auto or also during regular Bluetooth calls. This comparison can help narrow down the issue.

With the vehicle safely parked:

  • Restart your phone and Sync, then try another call.
  • If you use a wireless adapter, disconnect it and test with a direct USB connection.
  • Disconnect Android Auto and compare a call using Bluetooth only.
  • If possible, try another compatible phone.

If the echo continues, please contact us with your order number, vehicle’s year and model, phone model, Sync software version and the results of these checks.

Please contact us before changing the APIM software or replacing hardware. We have not confirmed one fix that applies to every case.

articles.body:
Buttons pressing themselves, menus opening or the screen scrolling without being touched are often called “phantom touches.” This can indicate a problem with the digitizer, the touch-sensitive layer of the display.

Damage may not always be visible. Please contact us with your order number, vehicle’s year and model, and a description of what is happening. Let us know whether the problem started immediately after installation or developed later.

articles.title: Why won’t my USB hub bezel stay clipped in?
articles.body:
The bezel’s retaining tabs need enough material around the opening to hold it securely. If the opening is damaged or does not provide enough material for the tabs to grip, the bezel may not stay clipped in.

articles.title: Why won’t Apple CarPlay or Android Auto connect?
articles.body:
Start by testing a direct USB connection with a known good data cable. If you use a wireless adapter, disconnect it while troubleshooting.

  1. Check the cable. Use an authentic Apple or Samsung cable, or a high quality cable that specifically supports data transfer. A phone charging does not necessarily mean the data connection is working.
  2. Check the phone’s connection. Make sure the plug seats fully and inspect the charging port for lint or debris.
  3. Restart your phone and Sync. Reconnect your phone, unlock it and accept any CarPlay or Android Auto permission prompts.
  4. Try another compatible phone and cable. This helps determine whether the issue follows your phone or remains with the vehicle.
  5. If needed, follow our reset instructions. Start with a soft reset. A master reset clears saved settings and paired phones, so you will need to set those up again afterward.

You can find our reset instructions on the installation page.

Still having trouble? Contact us with your order number, vehicle’s year and model, phone model, and the results of these checks. Please mention whether the connection previously worked and whether you are using a standard USB hub, wireless adapter or hub with built in wireless connectivity.

articles.title: Why is the climate control tab missing after my conversion?
articles.body:
The touchscreen climate control tab is not enabled for every vehicle. Its availability depends on your vehicle’s climate system, physical controls and APIM configuration.

If your physical climate controls work normally, a missing touchscreen tab does not necessarily indicate a problem. Enabling the tab also does not add features your vehicle is not equipped with.

Enabling the climate tab with FORScan

  1. Open the APIM’s Module configuration (AS BUILT format) in FORScan.
  2. Update the indicated positions below, leaving each position marked with an x unchanged.
  3. Write the changes and follow FORScan’s prompts to complete the procedure.
APIM lineValue
7D0-01-01xxxx - xxx3 - xxxx
7D0-01-02xxxx - x2xx - xxxx

Each “x” means keep the existing value in that position. Do not enter the letter x into FORScan.

Please contact us with your order number, vehicle’s year and model, and a photo of your climate control bezel if you need help.

articles.title: How do I connect my phone to the wireless USB-C hub?
articles.body:
Pair your phone directly with the wireless USB-C hub through your phone’s Bluetooth settings. The hub uses Bluetooth to establish the initial connection, then Wi-Fi for wireless Apple CarPlay or Android Auto.

These instructions apply to our USB-C hub with built-in wireless connectivity. Your infotainment system must be running Sync 3.4.

First-time setup

  1. With your vehicle safely parked, turn on your infotainment system and make sure the hub is installed and powered.
  2. Enable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on your phone.
  3. Open your phone’s Bluetooth settings and select the hub from the available devices. The Bluetooth name can vary between hubs.
  4. Accept the pairing request and any prompts to allow Apple CarPlay or Android Auto.
  5. Allow the connection to finish. CarPlay or Android Auto should then appear on your vehicle’s display.

Keep Wi-Fi enabled

The hub uses Wi-Fi for the CarPlay or Android Auto connection. Your phone may show a connection to a network with a name such as Sync3_xxxx. This is normal, and the network name may vary.

Bluetooth may disconnect after the Wi-Fi connection is established. This does not necessarily mean the hub has disconnected from your phone.

Charging while connected wirelessly

Use the upper USB-C port to charge your phone while using wireless CarPlay or Android Auto. Avoid connecting a phone to the lower USB-A port at the same time, as this can cause connection conflicts.

Need help getting connected?

Contact us with your order number, phone model and a description of what happens when you try to connect. Let us know whether the hub appears in Bluetooth settings and whether any message appears on your phone or vehicle’s display.

articles.title: How do I switch between phones on the wireless USB-C hub?
articles.body:
Disconnect the phone currently using wireless CarPlay or Android Auto before connecting the phone you want to use.

  1. On the currently connected phone, temporarily turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi in the phone’s Settings app.
  2. Wait for its CarPlay or Android Auto connection to close.
  3. On the phone you want to use, make sure Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are enabled.
  4. Open its Bluetooth settings and select the wireless hub. If this phone has not connected before, follow our first time pairing instructions and accept the CarPlay or Android Auto prompts.
  5. Allow the connection to finish before starting your trip.

For iPhone users: Use the Settings app when turning Bluetooth and Wi-Fi off. The buttons in Control Center do not fully turn these features off.

If the other phone keeps reconnecting

Leave Bluetooth and Wi-Fi disabled on that phone while establishing the connection with the phone you want to use. Remember to restore those settings afterward when appropriate.

If you still cannot switch phones, contact us with your order number, both phone models and a description of what happens.

articles.title: Why won’t my wireless USB-C hub reconnect to my phone?
articles.body:
Start by checking your phone’s settings and whether another phone is connecting to the hub. A connection problem does not necessarily mean the hub needs to be replaced.

These steps apply to our USB-C hub with built-in wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto.

1. Check Bluetooth and Wi-Fi

Make sure both are enabled in your phone’s Settings app. Wireless CarPlay and Android Auto use Bluetooth for the initial connection and Wi-Fi during operation.

For iPhone users, check that Auto-Join is enabled for the hub’s Wi-Fi network, if it appears in your Wi-Fi settings.

2. Rule out another phone connecting

If another previously paired phone is nearby, temporarily disable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on that phone, then try connecting yours again.

3. Check which USB port you’re using

Use the upper USB-C port for charging while connected wirelessly. Disconnect any phone connected to the lower USB-A port, as this can cause connection conflicts.

4. Restart and try again

Restart your phone and infotainment system, then try reconnecting. Check your phone for any prompts requesting permission to use CarPlay or Android Auto.

5. Pair the phone again

If the problem continues, remove the hub’s saved Bluetooth pairing from your phone and follow our first time pairing instructions again.

For iPhone users, you may also need to remove the corresponding connection under Settings → General → CarPlay → Forget This Car before setting it up again.

6. Try another compatible phone

If another phone connects successfully, that helps narrow the issue to the original phone’s settings, software or saved connection. Let us know the results if you contact us.

Still having trouble?

Contact us with your order number, phone model and software version. Tell us whether the hub never connects, fails to reconnect after starting the vehicle, or disconnects while you’re using it.

Also mention whether the issue started after a phone update and which steps you have already tried. We can help determine whether a hub firmware update or another check is appropriate.
